EVIDENCE PACK
expectation_key: imp-career
section: impact_section
pack_status: complete

=== PROSE SPANS (verbatim from the section under assessment) ===

[span 2.1¶1]
The Doctoral Network will establish a pan-European training ecosystem for causal AI in healthcare, integrating academic, clinical, industrial and regulatory stakeholders into a coherent framework. It contributes directly to the MSCA objective of structuring doctoral education by embedding a common curriculum, interoperable learning modules and shared infrastructures across universities, hospitals, technology and data providers, and policy or regulatory bodies.

[span 2.1¶4]
The network promotes international, intersectoral and interdisciplinary mobility. DCs enrol in accredited programmes in EU Member States or Associated Countries, receiving co-supervision from academic and non-academic sectors.

[span 2.1¶5]
All DCs will complete a substantial secondment (4-6 months) in another sector, typically hosted by non-academic partners (hospitals, SMEs, large industry or regulatory/standardisation bodies). Supervisors from these organisations sit on the Supervisory Board and Individual Training Panels (ITP). This ensures exposure to the non- academic sector, enhances employability, provides complementary supervision and creates networking opportunities.

[span 2.1¶6]
Cross-sectoral and cross-national mobility is further supported by international secondments between clinical and data-science environments, creating long-term institutional links between academic and non-academic partners and building a pipeline of intersectoral research careers.

[span 2.1¶7]
Measurable outcomes include at least three joint doctoral courses, three transferable- skills modules and the majority (≥ 80%) of secondment months in non-academic settings.

[span 2.1¶14]
These elements directly reinforce European innovation capacity and prepare DCs for non-academic careers across med-tech, hospitals, regulatory bodies and digital-health start-ups.

[span 2.1¶18]
The AI knowledge hub, aligned with standards such as ResearchComp and ESG, serves as a Horizon Europe reference point and disseminates materials on AI Act and EHDS implementation. An Europe-wide alumni hub and an Innovation and Sustainability Committee will track indicators such as joint publications, IP, follow-up projects and external users of academy resources, and will adapt the programme where needed.

[span 2.2¶0]
Career development is a key priority, anchored in the Training and Career Development work package. Within their first three months, each Doctoral Candidate (DC) establishes a Personal Career Development Plan (PCDP) with their supervisory team, detailing research milestones, scientific and transferable-skills targets, secondments, teaching and outreach contributions, and short-, medium- and long-term career objectives. PCDPs are reviewed annually and used to adapt training and mobility activities to evolving interests and labour-market trends.

[span 2.2¶1]
Every fellow is supported by a PhD committee comprising at least one academic supervisor, one non-academic or clinical supervisor and, where relevant, a representative from the secondment host. This multi-mentor structure provides consistent guidance and impartial advice on academic, clinical, industrial and policy careers, and facilitates early identification of additional skills or networking needs. Training progress and PCDPs are monitored through dedicated reporting and structured feedback mechanisms.

[span 2.2¶2]
Combining methodological innovation in causal and trustworthy AI with real-world constraints such as data quality, workflow integration, interoperability and regulatory documentation prepares graduates to lead multidisciplinary teams in hospitals, industry R&D departments, start-ups and research infrastructures. This unique profile is difficult to obtain in single-discipline programmes and significantly enhances employability.

[span 2.2¶3]
Triple-I exposure and professional networks

[span 2.2¶4]
Triple-I exposure (international, intersectoral and interdisciplinary) increases DCs’ visibility, experience with clinical, product-development and regulatory workflows, and their ability to combine technical, clinical, legal and human factors in practice.

[span 2.2¶5]
Transferable skills, innovation, entrepreneurship and regulatory literacy

[span 2.2¶6]
The transferable-skills programme embedded in the training and impact work packages equips DCs with strong competences in:

[span 2.2¶7]
• project and time management;

[span 2.2¶8]
• teamwork and leadership;

[span 2.2¶9]
• scientific and non-technical communication;

[span 2.2¶10]
• intercultural collaboration;

[span 2.2¶11]
• stress and conflict management.

[span 2.2¶12]
Training in IP protection, entrepreneurship, innovation management and the use of a Research-to-Innovation (R2I) canvas enables fellows to identify and articulate the scientific, technological and societal value of their work.

[span 2.2¶13]
Positioning for diverse and sustainable career paths

[span 2.2¶14]
These elements position DCs for sustainable careers:

[span 2.2¶15]
• in academia and research infrastructures as experts in causal and trustworthy AI for health;

[span 2.2¶16]
• in hospitals and healthcare providers as clinical data scientists and digital-health leaders;

[span 2.2¶17]
• in industry and start-ups as specialists in trustworthy, regulation-ready AI;

[span 2.2¶18]
• as advisors to regulatory agencies, policy bodies and professional societies.

[span 2.2¶19]
The network’s long-term AI knowledge hub will provide a lasting platform for showcasing fellows’ outputs and profiles and maintaining an alumni network, thereby extending the impact of the training beyond the project lifetime and supporting continued cross-sector mobility.

[span 2.3¶7]
Joint sessions at major international conferences, dedicated symposia on trustworthy AI in healthcare and cross-sector workshops involving clinical and regulatory stakeholders will ensure that project results reach both academic and applied communities.

[span 2.4¶8]
The project will strengthen knowledge transfer between data science, clinical practice and the digital-health sector by producing validated and interoperable AI methods that reduce development risks and support adoption by hospitals, SMEs and technology providers.

=== CLAIM-LEDGER ENTRIES: none - the ledger is withheld from this lane; grounding is UNASSESSABLE from this pack ===

3. `query-docs` with the selected library ID and the user's full question (not single words)
4. Answer using the fetched docs
